blocks.content: Before you can fix high cardinality, you need to see it. This guide shows you how to read the Cardinality tab in Cost Management and Billing, then review Adaptive Metrics recommendations so you can reduce series without reinstrumenting your services.

You need the `grafana-cmab-app.cardinality:read` permission for the Cardinality tab ([CMAB RBAC](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/cost-management-and-billing/set-up/cost-management-billing-rbac/)) and Adaptive Metrics read access for recommendations ([Adaptive Metrics RBAC](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/adaptive-telemetry/adaptive-metrics/additional-configuration/adaptive-metrics-rbac/)). A stack that is already receiving metrics shows richer data.
In this section, you'll open the Cardinality tab and identify your highest-cardinality metrics and labels.
Open the **Usage** tab of the Cost Management and Billing app.
Select the **Cardinality** tab.

Review the summary stats at the top: **Unique metrics**, **Total active series**, **Unique labels**, and **Total label value pairs**. **Total active series** is the number your metrics bill is based on.

In the **Highest cardinality metrics** table, the **Series** column shows how many active series each metric produces, and **% Total** shows its share of your stack's series count. Start your investigations here: these metrics contribute the most to cost.
Review the **Highest cardinality labels** table. Labels with many distinct values, such as IDs or addresses, are the multiplication factors that inflate your series count.

Check the **Status** column for **New** and **Unused** badges. A **New** badge marks a metric or label first ingested in the last 30 days. An **Unused** badge marks a metric that isn't used in queries, dashboards, recording rules, or alerting rules, so it may be costing you without providing value.

Open a metric row to see its details drawer: cardinality history, label breakdown, query count, and the dashboards and rules that reference it. The **Actions** menu links to deeper analysis and remediation, including Adaptive Metrics.

You've identified which metrics and labels drive your active series count. Ask: which metrics produce the most series, which labels have the most unique values, and is anything both high-cardinality and unused?

Adaptive Metrics can reduce cardinality from inside Grafana Cloud by aggregating away labels nobody uses, while keeping the metric and your existing dashboards, rules, and queries working. You can reverse an aggregation later if usage changes.
In this section, you'll open Adaptive Metrics and review recommendations for your stack.
In the navigation menu, expand **Adaptive Telemetry**. If the section is already expanded, skip this step.
Navigate to **Adaptive Metrics** and open the **Metrics** tab.

steps.tooltip: Open the Adaptive Metrics app from the navigation.
Open the Metrics view to see recommendations for your stack.

blocks.content: Review the recommendations table. Each row shows which metric it affects and which labels it proposes to aggregate away, based on how the metric is actually used.
Open a recommendation to review its details before applying it, including the recommended rule information and the metric's usage stats.
You've reviewed Adaptive Metrics recommendations and how each one proposes to reduce cardinality without changing your ingestion pipeline.

Recommended remediation order:

1. **Address unused metrics.** Metrics with the **Unused** badge in the Cardinality tab add cost with no value.
2. **Assess high-cardinality labels on used metrics.** Aggregate away label dimensions nobody queries, and keep the ones they do.
3. **Protect what matters.** Define exemptions for metrics that must never be aggregated.

For a fuller CMAB tour, see [Understand billing and usage](https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/billing-usage/). For the complete Adaptive Metrics workflow (rules, exemptions, segmentation, auto-apply), see [Optimize metrics with Adaptive Metrics](https://grafana.com/docs/learning-paths/adaptive-metrics/).

Docs: [Historical metrics cardinality](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/cost-management-and-billing/analyze-costs/metrics-costs/prometheus-metrics-costs/historical-cardinality/), [Manage recommendations](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/adaptive-telemetry/adaptive-metrics/manage-recommendations/).
